## Supplied failures

These functions are deliberately broken. Keep them as evidence.

```{r}
pooled_mean <- function(x) sum(x) / length(x)
summarise_change <- function(x) pooled_mean(x)
report_change <- function(data) summarise_change(data$change)
bad_data <- data.frame(change = c("-2", "1", "0"))
broken_mean <- function(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE) / length(x)
broken_change <- function(baseline, followup) followup - baseline
```

## 1–2. Symptoms and minimal example

```{r}
mean(c("2", "4"))
try(report_change(bad_data), silent = TRUE)
broken_mean(c(2, NA, 4))
# TODO: record expected versus actual behavior and shrink the nested error.
```

## 3. Console-only inspection

Run the lines below interactively, not while rendering. At the browser prompt,
inspect `str(x)` and exit with `Q`. Then describe what you found.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
report_change(bad_data)
traceback()
debugonce(pooled_mean)
report_change(bad_data)
```

## 5. Numerical reliability

```{r}
0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3
isTRUE(all.equal(0.1 + 0.2, 0.3))
all.equal(1, 2)
# Overflow in integer arithmetic; the double result is exact at this size.
.Machine$integer.max + 1L
.Machine$integer.max + 1
# Avoid forming a product that underflows before taking its logarithm.
log(prod(rep(0.01, 200)))
sum(log(rep(0.01, 200)))
```
